description: Compulsory military service after his Abitur, trained in the self-propelled artillery; his last rank was Fahnenjunker (officer cadet).
Probationary judge at the local court in Saarbrücken after his second state law examination.

organization: Verband der Chemischen Industrie (VCI), Bonn and Frankfurt am Main
description: Worked for the German chemical industry association; admitted as a lawyer (Rechtsanwalt) since 1986.
Elected in the 1989 European election for the CDU in North Rhine-Westphalia; sat on the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs.

role: Member of the Bundestag (directly elected, Hochsauerlandkreis)
description: Won the Hochsauerlandkreis constituency four times (1994, 1998, 2002, 2005); initially a finance-policy specialist (CDU/CSU lead member on the finance committee 1996–1998), later a member of the legal affairs committee (2005–2009). He announced in 2007 that he would not stand again and left parliament in October 2009.

role: Deputy chairman of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group
description: Deputy leader of the CDU/CSU group in opposition to the Schröder government.

role: Chairman of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group and Leader of the Opposition
description: Succeeded Wolfgang Schäuble as group leader and was thus Leader of the Opposition during Gerhard Schröder's first term. After the 2002 election, CDU leader Angela Merkel claimed the group chairmanship for herself.

role: Deputy chairman of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group
description: Deputy to group leader Angela Merkel; he resigned the post in December 2004, ending his long-running power struggle with her.

Corporate lawyer at the international law firm (M&A, banking and finance, compliance). According to his Bundestag biography he was partner from 2005 to 2014 and senior counsel from 2014 to 2021 (the federal government's CV gives 2017 for the switch); his Bundestag disclosures list the role as ending on 31 December 2021. Before joining Mayer Brown he worked as a lawyer for a Cologne firm alongside his mandate.
Chaired the private non-profit association that promotes German-American and transatlantic relations.

role: Mandated manager of the WestLB sale process
description: Commissioned by the federal bank-rescue fund to manage the sale of the state bank WestLB to a private investor; the sale did not take place and his reported fee drew media criticism.

Chaired the supervisory board of the German subsidiary of the US asset manager. He gave up the post in 2020, the year of his second bid for the CDU leadership, and BlackRock named a successor (Handelsblatt).

organization: Wirtschaftsrat der CDU e.V. (CDU-affiliated business association)
description: Vice-president of the business association close to the CDU, after losing the December 2018 CDU leadership vote.

role: Member of the Bundestag (directly elected, Hochsauerlandkreis)
description: Returned to the Bundestag after winning the Hochsauerlandkreis constituency in 2021 and again in 2025. His law practice has been dormant since 25 March 2025 according to his disclosures.
Elected CDU leader after winning a membership ballot in December 2021 and being confirmed by a digital party congress on 22 January 2022; re-elected in May 2024 and, with 91.2%, in February 2026.

role: Chairman of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group and Leader of the Opposition
description: Succeeded Ralph Brinkhaus as leader of the largest opposition group during the Scholz government; named the CDU/CSU chancellor candidate in September 2024. Succeeded by Jens Spahn when he became chancellor.

Elected tenth Chancellor of the Federal Republic on 6 May 2025 in a second ballot (325 votes) after failing in the first (310 votes, 316 needed), the first such failure in the Federal Republic's history. He heads a CDU/CSU–SPD coalition with Lars Klingbeil (SPD) as Vice-Chancellor and Finance Minister. As of October 2026 the government is in a crisis marked by record-low approval ratings, CDU defeats in the September 2026 state elections and the resignation of Labour Minister Bärbel Bas on 12 October 2026, who was succeeded by Alexander Schweitzer.
